_comment: Phase 1 matrix vs REAL repo. Recon (T0/T2) confirmed real prefixes are /api/techscape/v1/* and /api/travel/v1/* (NOT /api/techscape/* — the router mount adds /v1). 'admin' column below is the spec's branch-admin tier, which core/deps.py stores as role='manager' (bare 'admin' is reserved for the legacy top rank == super_admin — see core/deps.py docstring). Token minting REQUIRES --biz <active business id> AND --sub <real ts_users id whose actual DB role matches the column> — core/deps.get_current_user re-reads the DB row and ignores the token's role claim, so access_matrix.py's mint() must be given real per-role user ids via the GOGAGA_SUB_* env vars. (Historical note: mint() once passed no --sub/--biz at all; that was fixed in commit acdf499 during Phase 1, and this comment previously still described the broken behaviour as current.) Wiki uses 201/204 on create/delete; users/branches use 201 on create.
_notes: leads.py's assigned-only scoping (Phase 2 T1) is DONE — agent-tier GET/list is restricted to assigned_agent=self, manager+ stays business-wide. Status-code matrix above still shows 200/200/200/403 for GET (all non-viewer roles get 200; the ROW-LEVEL filtering isn't a status-code difference) — row-level proof needs real per-agent fixtures with different assignments, done in PHASE2_REPORT.md T1/T7 evidence, not this static spec.

calls.py (Phase 2 T7) mirrors the same pattern via lead_id join: agent-tier GET /calls/live returns only calls whose lead is assigned to them (still 200, filtered result). GET /calls/{id}/transcript and the WS /ws/calls/{call_id} live feed depend on a specific call's scope (in/out of the caller's assignment) — not expressible as a static per-role code here, verified via real fixtures in PHASE2_REPORT.md instead.

PATCH/DELETE target-id tests, out-of-branch 404s, role-elevation 403s, and the token-invalidation chain were verified in T3-T5 (Phase 1) and T1/T7 (Phase 2) task chains with real per-role DB fixtures (not this static spec) — see PHASE1_REPORT.md / PHASE2_REPORT.md.
logout is tested separately from the table above in practice (each call invalidates that role's own token) — run it last per role, not interleaved with the other rows.

webhooks_voice.py's POST /webhook/{provider}/voice and WS /webhook/{provider}/stream are NOT in this matrix — they use Plivo-signature auth, not JWT/roles, so a per-role expectation table doesn't apply. See PHASE2_REPORT.md for their verification (HMAC signature logic + simulated frame sequences).

ai-config (Phase 3 T2, added this sprint 2026-08-07): GET is require_role('viewer') so every authenticated role passes; PUT/seed are require_role('manager') so only admin(=manager)/super_admin pass. GET/seed auto-create a default config row on first access, so PUT is safe to re-run across sweeps (idempotent update, not insert). takeover.py's /calls/{id}/takeover/* and /calls/{id}/events ARE now in this matrix (Phase 3 T10), using the all-zeros UUID as a deliberately nonexistent call. That covers the two outcomes that ARE static: viewer is rejected at require_role('agent') with 403 before any lookup, and agent+ get a clean 404 from the scope check rather than a 500. The state-dependent outcomes — 200 on a real active call, 409 on a non-active one, and the assigned-vs-unassigned 404 split for agent-tier — still need real fixtures and a live call, so they are NOT asserted here.

GET /calls/{id}/events had an authorization bypass until Phase 3 T10: it called get_call_scoped() but discarded the result, and get_call_scoped RETURNS None rather than raising. Any agent-tier user could read any call's event log, including cross-tenant, since get_events() filters on call_id alone. The 404 rows above are the regression test for that fix.
